what_to_detect: A targeting candidate whose targeting clause names no zone has only battlefield permanents (and players) in its legal_targets; cards of the matching type in other zones are absent.
near_miss: A candidate whose clause names another zone (a graveyard, the stack) has cards in that zone in its legal_targets.
record_fields: decision candidates[].legal_targets
snapshot entity zone of each listed target
acting line ValidTgts$/TgtZone$

what_to_detect: An 'any target' candidate's legal_targets lists no permanent that is not a creature, planeswalker or battle: such a permanent on the battlefield is outside the list.
near_miss: A creature, player, planeswalker or battle inside an 'any target' candidate's legal_targets.
record_fields: decision candidates[].legal_targets
snapshot battlefield entities and their types
acting line ValidTgts$ Any

what_to_detect: A target-changing ability resolves and the retargeted spell's targets after it differ from its targets before it: a change is made only where another legal target exists.
near_miss: A target-changing ability resolves and the retargeted spell keeps the targets it had, because no other legal target exists.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: An ability that changes the target of a spell resolves and exactly one of that spell's targets differs afterwards, the new one legal.
near_miss: Such an ability resolves and the spell's targets are unchanged, because the only possible new target was illegal or already a target of it.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: An ability that changes any targets resolves and one or more of the spell's targets differ afterwards, the resulting target set legal.
near_miss: Such an ability resolves and the spell's targets are unchanged, because the proposed target set was illegal.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: An ability that chooses new targets for a spell resolves and the targets it changed are legal ones, a target left unchanged possibly still illegal.
near_miss: Such an ability resolves and a target is left as it was because the proposed new one was illegal.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: A target-changing ability resolves and the spell's targets afterwards are a reordering or replacement checked only as a final legal set (two targets swapped).
near_miss: Such an ability resolves and the targets are unchanged because the final set would name one object twice for distinct-target slots.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: A retargeted spell with divided damage or counters keeps each share with its slot: the new target carries the old target's per_target_amounts share.
near_miss: The retargeted divided spell's targets and shares are unchanged (the change was declined).
record_fields: state.entities[].stack_extras.per_target_amounts of the retargeted spell before the clause
the retargeted spell's later snapshot stack_extras.per_target_amounts
targets_changed event params.targets

what_to_detect: A target-changing ability resolves on a modal spell and its target differs afterwards, the new target legal for the chosen mode.
near_miss: Such an ability resolves on a modal spell and its target is unchanged, because the proposed target is legal only for an unchosen mode.
record_fields: targets_changed event params.targets (written on every ChangeTargets resolution, changed or not)
the retargeted spell's stack_extras / refs.targets in the snapshot before the clause

what_to_detect: A cast trigger conditioned on a spell with a single target is evaluated and fires for a spell with exactly one target.
near_miss: The same trigger is evaluated and does not fire because the spell has more than one target, repeats counted.
record_fields: trigger payload.fired
trigger line's ValidSA$ (singleTarget) through the sidecar
state.refs.targets of the cast spell

what_to_detect: A spell that targets a spell restricted by what that spell targets resolves because the targeted spell still targets a matching object, even one that became an illegal target.
near_miss: Such a spell fizzles because the targeted spell's target has left its zone and no longer counts.
record_fields: cost half payload.outcome
state.refs.targets
acting line TargetValidTargeting$ through the sidecar
stack_extras.targets of the targeted spell

what_to_detect: A cast trigger conditioned on a spell that targets only one object is evaluated and fires for a spell whose targets are one distinct object, chosen once or more.
near_miss: The same trigger is evaluated and does not fire because the spell targets two or more distinct objects.
record_fields: trigger payload.fired
trigger line's IsSingleTarget$ through the sidecar
state.refs.targets of the cast spell
